nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Sustainable agriculture|Livestock waste management_qna_000
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How does the environmental impact of mycoprotein compare to beef, chicken, and pork?
nodes.answer: Life-cycle analyses suggest that mycoprotein has a lower environmental impact than beef and similar impact to chicken and pork, with the highest impacts from energy and emissions, and negligible impacts from eutrophication and land use.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Sustainable agriculture|Livestock waste management_qna_001
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: How much manure was produced by the 560 cattle in year 1?
nodes.answer: The manure production was 18.0 Mg fresh matter (FM).
nodes.paragraph: The cover crops were a mixture of clover and ryegrass. The other 500 hectares included grass-clover grazing, grass clover silage production, and pea-spring barley for silage (rotation 2). This area was considered out- side of the system boundary as it was assumed not to be affected by the actions in rotation 1. The manure production of the 560 cattle was 18,0 Mg fresh matter (FM) year 1, with 49.1 g N kg 1 dry matter (DM) (Fontaine et al. 2020b). Assuming 189 grazing days (6 h day 1), 15,600 Mg are collected in the animal house and stored to be field applied. This results in 27.7 Mg ha 1 applied to the spring barley in rotation 1. Of the barley produced, 1,344 Mg grains are used for feed, and 336 Mg straw is needed for feed and bedding. Any additional barley grain production was assumed to be sold and is modelled to substitute other organic barley production at the market, using data from the Ecoin- vent database (Wernet et al. 2016).

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Sustainable agriculture|Livestock waste management_qna_002
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: Why is the effective management of manure in livestock production crucial for reducing GHG emissions?
nodes.answer: Efficient management of manure, including solid-liquid separation and dry solids' management, is important as GHG emissions from manure management significantly contribute to the overall GHG footprint of meat products throughout their lifecycle.
